Grammatik
☀️ Present Simple üben: Tagesablauf, he / she / it + -s, Sams Tag (zum Öffnen tippen)
📋 Gesamtübersicht: alle Zeitformen als Tabelle (zum Öffnen tippen)
V = Grundform (go, work) V2 = Simple Past (went, worked) V3 = Partizip (gone, worked) S = Subjekt  O = Objekt
Ein Verb, alle Zeiten: watch. Für jede Zeit: Beispiel · Wann? · Signalwörter. Ganz unten: Kurzformen, Spelling-Regeln und typische Fehler.

⬅️ Past (Vergangenheit)

TenseBeispielWann? · 🔑 Signalwörter
Past SimpleI watched TV.abgeschlossen, fertig
🔑 yesterday, ago, last week, in 2010
Past ContinuousI was watching TV at 8pm.lief gerade, wurde unterbrochen
🔑 while, when, at 8pm yesterday
Past PerfectI had watched it before.noch vor einer anderen Vergangenheit
🔑 before, after, already, by the time
Past Perf. Cont.I had been watching for 2 hours.Dauer bis zu einem Punkt in der Vergangenheit
🔑 for, since, all day (bis damals)

⏺️ Present (Gegenwart)

TenseBeispielWann? · 🔑 Signalwörter
Present SimpleI watch TV every day.
She watches TV.		Gewohnheit, Fakt
🔑 every day, always, usually, often, never
Present ContinuousI am watching TV now.gerade jetzt, vorübergehend
🔑 now, at the moment, today, Look!
Present PerfectI have watched this film.Erfahrung, Verbindung zu jetzt
🔑 already, yet, ever, never, just, for, since
Pres. Perf. Cont.I have been watching for 1 hour.Dauer bis jetzt
🔑 for, since, all day, how long

➡️ Future (Zukunft)

FormBeispielWann? · 🔑 Signalwörter
willI will watch it tomorrow.
I'll answer it!		spontan, Versprechen, Vorhersage (Meinung)
🔑 tomorrow, I think, probably
going toI am going to watch it tonight.schon geplant · Vorhersage mit Beweis
🔑 tonight, next week, Look at …!
Pres. ContinuousI am watching it on Saturday.fester Termin, verabredet
🔑 on Saturday, at 7pm, tomorrow

✅ ❌ ❓ Positiv · Negativ · Frage

Tense✅ Positiv❌ Negativ❓ Frage
Present SimpleI watch / she watchesI don't watch / she doesn't watchDo you watch? / Does she watch?
Present ContinuousI'm watchingI'm not watchingAre you watching?
Past SimpleI watchedI didn't watchDid you watch?
Past ContinuousI was / we were watchingI wasn't / we weren't watchingWere you watching?
Present PerfectI have / she has watchedI haven't / she hasn't watchedHave you watched?
willI'll watchI won't watchWill you watch?
going toI'm going to watchI'm not going to watchAre you going to watch?
will vs. going to
spontan → will · schon entschieden → going to
"The phone is ringing!" — "I'll answer it!"
"I'm going to call him later."
Fester Termin mit Uhrzeit/Tag → Present Continuous: "We're flying to London on Monday."
Past Continuous + Past Simple
lange Aktion (was/were + -ing) + kurze Aktion (V2)
"While I was watching TV, my phone rang."
"She was cooking when he came home."
while + Past Continuous (Hintergrund) · when + Past Simple (unterbricht)
am / is / are
Subject + am/is/are + verb-ing
I am · he/she/it is · you/we/they are
I am watching TV. · She is reading a book. · They are learning English.
did / didn't + Grundform
Negativ & Frage im Past Simple: did + V
❌ She didn't went. ✅ She didn't go.
Die Vergangenheit steckt schon in "did" — das Verb bleibt in der Grundform.

✂️ Kurzformen (Short forms)

LangKurzNegativ
I amI'mI'm not
you areyou'reyou aren't
he / she / it ishe's / she's / it'she isn't / she isn't / it isn't
we / they arewe're / they'rewe aren't / they aren't
was / were not—wasn't / weren't
do / does / did not—don't / doesn't / didn't
have / hasI've / she'shaven't / hasn't
willI'll / you'llwon't (= will not)

🔤 Spelling-Regeln (-ing)

Regel-ing
normalplay → playing
stummes -e fällt wegcome → coming
kurz: Konsonant doppeltsit → sitting
Konsonant + ystudy → studying
-ie → -ylie → lying
Typische Fehler: ❌ I m reading → ✅ I'm reading · "I" immer groß, Nomen klein (a book, football) · ❌ She didn't went → ✅ She didn't go · ❌ Have you seen it yesterday? → ✅ Did you see it yesterday? · enjoy + -ing: ✅ I'm enjoying playing football.
Grundregel: Englisch = Subject + Verb + Object (SVO). Das Verb steht immer an 2. Stelle.
Satzbau
S + V + O + (Place) + (Time)
"She reads books at home every day."
„Sie liest jeden Tag zu Hause Bücher."
Ort vor Zeit; Häufigkeitsadverbien vor dem Verb
If-Clause Type 1
If + Simple Present, … will + V
"If it rains, we will cancel the trip."
„Wenn es regnet, sagen wir die Reise ab."
Reale, mögliche Situation in der Zukunft
möglich · wahrscheinlich
If-Clause Type 2
If + Simple Past, … would + V
"If I had more money, I would travel."
„Wenn ich mehr Geld hätte, würde ich reisen."
Hypothetische / unwahrscheinliche Situation
unreal · hypothetisch
If-Clause Type 3
If + Past Perfect, … would have + V3
"If I had studied, I would have passed."
„Wenn ich gelernt hätte, hätte ich bestanden."
Verpasste Möglichkeit in der Vergangenheit
irreale Vergangenheit
Relative Clause
… who / which / that + V …
"The man who called is my boss."
„Der Mann, der angerufen hat, ist mein Chef."
who = Personen · which = Dinge · that = beides
Contact Clause
… (ohne Relativpronomen) + V …
"The book (that) I read was great."
„Das Buch, das ich gelesen habe, war toll."
Relativpronomen kann wegfallen, wenn es Objekt ist
Participle Construction
V-ing / V3 … (statt Relativsatz)
"The woman sitting there is my teacher."
„Die Frau, die dort sitzt, ist meine Lehrerin."
Kurzform des Relativsatzes · formeller Stil
Satzbau: Die 4 häufigsten Fehler
S + V + O · Do/Does/Did + S + V? · don't/doesn't/didn't + V · Simple Present vs. Progressive
"I go to school every day." ✓ — "I go every day to school." ✗
„Deutsch: Verb kann ans Ende — Englisch: Verb bleibt auf Platz 2"
"Do you like coffee?" ✓ — "You like coffee?" ✗
„Fragen immer mit Do/Does/Did beginnen (außer bei be/have)"
"I don't know." ✓ — "I know not." ✗
„Verneinung: don't/doesn't/didn't + Grundform"
"I work here." (Fakt) vs. "I am working now." (gerade jetzt)
„Simple Present = Gewohnheit · Progressive = gerade passierend"
1. Wortstellung: S+V+O · 2. Fragen: Do/Does/Did · 3. Verneinung: don't/doesn't · 4. Zeiten: Simple vs. -ing
S + V + O · Do? · don't · -ing jetzt

ZeitformFormelBeispiel

Wichtige Phrasal Verbs

Phrasal VerbBedeutungBeispiel

Steigerung der Adjektive
kurz: -er/-est · lang: more/most
fast → faster → the fastest
interesting → more interesting → the most interesting
Unregelmäßig: good→better→best · bad→worse→worst
much / many / a lot of
much + unzählbar · many + zählbar
"How much time?" / "How many people?"
a lot of geht mit beiden; much/many in Fragen & Verneinungen
little/few (wenig) · a little/a few (etwas)
Gerund vs. Infinitiv
V-ing = Gerund · to + V = Infinitiv
"I enjoy swimming." / "I want to swim."
enjoy/finish/avoid + Gerund · want/need/decide + Infinitiv
+ Gerund (-ing)
enjoy · don't mind
consider · recommend
suggest · practise
give up · avoid

would like · try

refuse · manage
expect

Zeit · Ort · Richtung
at 7 o'clock · in January · on Monday · on the desk · in Berlin · at home · go to work

📌 Mein Lernen
Hier landen automatisch alle Vokabeln und Fragen, die du falsch beantwortet hast (Karten „Nochmal“, Tages-Quiz, Prüfung), und die Wörter, die du in den Karten mit ✓ gewusst hast. Sie kommen nach Plan wieder: nach 1, 3, 7 und 14 Tagen (falsch = sofort wieder von vorn). Wer alle Stufen schafft, hat das Wort gelernt.
➕ Neues Wort
💾 Sicherung herunterladen
Speichert deinen Fortschritt, die Fehlerliste, dein Wörterbuch und deine Einstellungen in einer Datei. Damit kannst du alles auf ein neues Handy übertragen oder nach dem Löschen des Browsers wiederherstellen.
📂 Sicherung wiederherstellen
